newsitem.title: USA: South Dakota governor signs $1.9 bln budget.
newsitem.headline: South Dakota governor signs $1.9 bln budget.

text.p: - South Dakota Gov. William Janklow signed a $1.9 billion all-funds, fiscal 1998 budget into law on Tuesday.

The spending plan, which includes a $706 million general fund budget for the fiscal year that begins July 1, continues a 20 percent property tax cut started in the current fiscal year, according to Tyler Stowater, deputy commissioner of the state's bureau of finance and management.
Stowater said the budget fully funds the tax cut for local governments through state aid payments.
He added that the budget Janklow proposed in December was only minimally changed by lawmakers, who ended their legislative session earlier this month.
The fiscal 1998 budget will have no cash balance, but will have a statutory budget reserve of $24.6 million at the end of the fiscal year, Stowater said.
